Policy reading
The FY2024–25 portfolio redirects policy attention away from Pakistan’s established top export lines and toward the next layer of scalable capabilities. Policy should be organised around product missions, with public support and guarantee finance linked to specific testing, traceability, processing, tooling, certification, market-access and buyer-finance gaps—not generic export subsidies.

How to interpret unit values
Comparable lens
Unit values are realised export values divided by source quantities; they reflect grade, processing, packaging, contract terms, destination and product mix. Products measured in numbers, pairs, dozens, square metres or grams should not be converted to US$/kg without a reliable physical bridge.
External benchmark
Every row links to the HS6 BACI/TradeWeave exporter comparison. Ten market-specific ITC comparisons are embedded numerically; other rows remain linked but unquantified where physical units or bulk extraction were not sufficiently comparable. No global price is fabricated.

Sixteen product missions

Section F

Selection change, methodology and audit

The dashboard retains a complete audit trail of the removed and replacement products and of the rules applied to the full 4,340-line source universe.

Removed from the former 100
Backfilled into the revised 100
Source
PBS D-10 exports by commodity and country, cumulative July 2024–June 2025. Source values are in PKR thousands; FY2024–25 US$ conversion uses the SBP annual-average exchange rate of PKR 279.3/US$.
Exclusions
Textiles HS 50–63; rice HS 1006 / descriptions; national top 20 HS8 lines; furnace oil HS 27101941; cement and clinker HS 2523.
Scenario
Product opportunity, scale, growth, diversification, price headroom, complexity and feasibility determine an indicative 1.05×–3.20× five-year mission path. Tobacco and unprocessed petroleum receive no demand-expansion subsidy.
International benchmark
10 product lines carry embedded market-specific ITC unit-value checks; all 100 carry HS6 BACI/TradeWeave links. PBS values remain in the source unit, while most international comparisons are US$/tonne.
Competitiveness methodology
Definitions and calculation rules
All growth metrics compare FY2024–25 with FY2023–24 using each year’s annual-average PKR/US$ conversion. Quantities retain the PBS statistical unit.

Absolute export growth contribution

FY25 export proceeds − FY24 export proceeds, reported in US$ million for each product and summed across the selected portfolio.

Volume and unit-value growth

Q25 / Q24 − 1 and UV25 / UV24 − 1. Unit value equals export proceeds divided by the relevant PBS quantity unit.

Price-versus-volume decomposition

Exact midpoint method: Volume = (Q25−Q24)×(P25+P24)/2; Price = (P25−P24)×(Q25+Q24)/2. The two effects sum to the change in proceeds.

New, retained and lost destinations

A product-market link is material at US$50,000 per year. New crosses above the threshold; retained remains above it; lost falls below it.

Top-market share and HHI

Top-market share is the largest destination’s share. HHI = Σ destination share² × 10,000. Negative changes indicate diversification.

Attainable price-uplift opportunity

FY25 proceeds × min(30%, internal price headroom × capture assumption). The editable capture assumption defaults to 25%; the cap prevents full-volume convergence from being treated as a forecast.

Source register
Data, conversion and comparison sources
The dashboard preserves the uploaded design system while rebuilding the analytical universe from FY2024–25 data.
Domestic product data
Uploaded PBS D-10 workbook: D-10_Export-0625.xlsx. Product and destination values are in PKR thousands; quantities retain the source statistical unit. See the PBS external trade portal ↗.
Unit dictionary
kg = kilogram; metric tonne = MT; litre = LTR; dozen = DOZ; pair = PAIR; number = NO; gross = GR; m² = square metre. US$/unit is not converted across incompatible physical bases.
Foreign-exchange conversion
FY2024–25 uses PKR 279.3/US$, the SBP yearly average. Open SBP statistical supplement ↗.
International comparison
HS6 exporter ladders use CEPII BACI 2024 ↗ and TradeWeave ↗. Embedded market-specific checks draw on PBC/ITC analysis ↗.
